summary: The Energy Efficiency Reform Act of 2026 amends the Energy Policy and Conservation Act to place new requirements and restrictions on the Department of Energy regarding energy conservation standards and test procedures for consumer products and commercial or industrial equipment. The bill voids specific existing energy conservation standards, sets procedural rules for the Department of Energy, defines significant energy savings, alters petition and standard-setting criteria, and addresses federal preemption of state and local fuel-use restrictions.

affected_groups.effect: Must follow strict procedural rules, meet rulemaking deadlines, adhere to defined criteria when setting or amending energy conservation standards, and coordinate reporting requirements with other agencies.
affected_groups.group: Secretary of Energy and Department of Energy

affected_groups.effect: Subject to updated standard-setting procedures, specific rules on component reporting, and protection against the elimination of consumer-valued product characteristics or fuel types.
affected_groups.group: Manufacturers of consumer products and commercial equipment

affected_groups.effect: Preempted from enacting or enforcing restrictions on fuel use, energy efficiency rules after federal standard revocation, or bans on the installation and use of covered products based on fuel source or air pollutant emissions.

key_provisions: Requires the Secretary of Energy to issue a final rule within 270 days for specific procedures and interpretations related to energy conservation standards and test procedures, and voids certain prior procedural rules if the deadline is missed.
Nullifies specific final rules for consumer furnaces and commercial water heating equipment issued by the Department of Energy.
Defines 'significant energy savings' as a reduction over a 30-year period of at least 10 percent in full fuel cycle energy use.

Prohibits the Secretary of Energy from prescribing new or amended energy conservation standards unless specific evidence is met, such as ensuring standards do not result in the unavailability of product features, reliability, lifetimes, sizes, or fuel types.
Preempts state and local laws, codes, or regulations that prohibit or restrict the installation, use, or fuel source of covered products, or require their removal based on air pollutant emissions.
Prohibits the Secretary of Energy from prescribing any new or amended energy conservation standards for distribution transformers.
missing_information: The full text or broader consequences of the referenced Code of Federal Regulations parts (such as 10 CFR part 430) beyond what is explicitly cited in the bill.
Specific budgetary or personnel impacts on the Department of Energy, the Federal Trade Commission, or the Environmental Protection Agency.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Energy Efficiency Reform Act of 2026 amends the Energy Policy and Conservation Act to place new requirements and restrictions on the Department of Energy regarding energy conservation standards and test procedures for consumer products and commercial or industrial equipment. The bill voids specific existing energy conservation standards, sets procedural rules for the Department of Energy, defines significant energy savings, alters petition and standard-setting criteria, and addresses federal preemption of state and local fuel-use restrictions.
summary_detail.significance: The bill modifies the statutory framework governing federal energy efficiency standards for appliances and equipment, scales back certain Department of Energy rulemaking authorities, voids specific active standards, and explicitly limits state and local authority to restrict product fuel sources or set separate efficiency rules.
